speakers.name: Chanel Richardson
speakers.bio:
Chanel Richardson is currently a Technical Program Manager within Google Cloud’s Information Security Department (Cloud CISO). She works on data strategies and solutions for the organization.

Outside of work, Chanel explores technologies and has a strong interest in the ephemera of the internet. She is exploring many ways to remix public domain works that can be found on the Internet Archive. One such set of explorations has led to the creation of “Archive Radio”, a series of composite videos, available on YouTube, combining footage and music found on the archive.

speakers.name: Sydney James Harcourt
speakers.bio:
Sydney James Harcourt, lead vocalist in Rhapsody on the Outlaw Ocean, is a stage and screen actor from Detroit, Michigan. He’s known for his work on and off Broadway, starring in productions like the cultural phenomenon Hamilton (original Broadway company and 1st replacement for Aaron Burr), Disney’s The Lion King (Simba), and Green Day’s American Idiot. In 2019 he was nominated for Drama Desk and Lortel Awards for originating the role of Joe Scott in the original American cast of Bob Dylan’s Girl From The North Country. He’s since originated the role of Rum Tum Tugger in the critically-acclaimed Cats: The Jellicle Ball Off and On Broadway.

You’ve seen him in films and TV series, from standard fare (Gone, NCIS: New Orleans, Elementary) to decidedly less standard (a self-harming boxer in musical film I’m Not Gay, the undead demon Edouard who provides eerie countertenor / soprano vocals in Netflix’s animated Castlevania: Nocturne). A Grammy award winner and sought-after New York vocalist, he has performed on some of the world’s finest concert stages, including Radio City Music Hall, Avery Fisher Hall (with the New York Philharmonic), and Carnegie Hall. He’s toured North America from coast to coast and played sold-out stadiums from Australia to Indonesia to Puerto Rico. In 2017 he was the featured artist at the US Open Finals live broadcast honoring the 50th anniversary of Billie Jean King’s Triple Crown. He opened the Museum of the American Revolution (introducing then-Vice President Joe Biden), was invited to perform at the White House at their Children’s Educational initiative, and is a go-to for tailoring unique theatrical/concert performances at corporate events and charitable galas.

speakers.name: Roshan Noorzai
speakers.bio:
Roshan Noorzai is a lecturer for the MA in Communication program at Johns Hopkins University. He is a multimedia journalist at Voice of America (VOA), the largest U.S. international broadcaster. Prior to joining VOA, he served as an Assistant Professor of Mass Communication at the American University of Sharjah, UAE, where he taught courses in Journalism and Media Studies. He has also worked as Public Information Officer with the United Nations and USAID in Afghanistan.

Roshan earned his PhD in Mass Communication from Ohio University. His dissertation focused on the role of media in the framing of the Afghan conflict. His areas of research interests include news framing, media and conflict, social media, and information and communication technologies for social change.

speakers.name: Dipali Mukhopadhyay
speakers.bio: Dipali Mukhopadhyay is Jacob Blaustein Associate Professor in International Organizations and Conflict Resolution at the Johns Hopkins University School of Advanced International Studies. She is the author of Warlords, Strongman Governors, and the State in Afghanistan (Cambridge University Press, 2014), which was short-listed for the biennial Central Eurasian Studies Society Book Award in the Social Sciences, and, with Kimberly Howe, Good Rebel Governance: Revolutionary Politics and Western Intervention in Syria (Cambridge University Press, 2023). Her scholarly work has also been published in the British Journal of Political Science; Conflict, Security, and Development; Economics and Politics; Foreign Affairs; International Negotiation; Perspectives on Politics; and a number of edited volumes. Her co-edited volume (with Anna Larson and Omar Sharifi), Power and Authority in Afghanistan: Rethinking Politics, Intervention, and Rule is forthcoming with Bloomsbury. Mukhopadhyay is currently working on her next book on sovereignty and state-building in the shadows of counterterrorism.

speakers.name: Kim Williams
speakers.bio:
Kim Williams founded the Fair Path Project to confront the silent epidemic of workplace bullying and to help employees reclaim dignity at work. A veteran HR executive and survivor of workplace abuse, she witnessed firsthand how toxic culture, gaslighting, and retaliation harm not only individuals but entire organizations.

Today, Kim is recognized nationally as a speaker, advocate, and thought leader dedicated to ending workplace abuse and building safer, more just workplaces for all.

speakers.name: Jasmine Styles
speakers.bio:
Jasmine Styles is an award-winning anchor/reporter who’s spent nearly 15 years in local television news. She joined 7News DC in March 2025 as the alert desk anchor for the evening newscasts.

The Orlando, Florida native graduated from The Florida State University in 2012 with a B.A. in Communications and a minor in Journalism through a co-op program with Florida A&M University.

She landed her first job right after graduation in Columbia, South Carolina. She’s also worked in Southeast Texas, Tampa, Florida, and Cincinnati, Ohio.

Jasmine is a dedicated member of the National Association of Black Journalists, serving as its treasurer 2023-2026. She’s also a member of SAG-AFTRA.

speakers.name: Holly Jonas
speakers.bio: Holly Jonas is the director of Mongabay’s network program and a freelance journalist. She has about 20 years of experience in the nonprofit sector, with a background in international environmental and human rights law. She also volunteers with several nonprofits in DC, including in the DC Environmental Film Festival’s advisory council.

speakers.name: Joanne Leedom-Ackerman
speakers.bio: Joanne Leedom-Ackerman is a novelist, short story writer, and journalist. Her fiction includes The Far Side of the Desert, Burning Distance, regional bestseller The Dark Path to the River and No Marble Angels. A former reporter for The Christian Science Monitor, Joanne has won awards for her nonfiction and published fiction, articles and essays in newspapers, magazines, and books.

speakers.name: Ben Conarck
speakers.bio: Ben Conarck is a local criminal justice reporter at The Washington Post. Before joining the Post in 2026, he worked at The Baltimore Banner, where he covered police, jails and prisons. Conarck has also worked at the Miami Herald, where his coverage of the condominium collapse in Surfside, Fla won the 2022 Pulitzer Prize for breaking news reporting.

speakers.name: Patrick Jaicomo
speakers.bio:
Patrick Jaicomo is a Senior Attorney at the Institute for Justice and one of the leaders of its Project on Immunity and Accountability. Through the project, Patrick works to dismantle judicially created immunity doctrines and ensure that individual rights are enforceable against the government and its agents. He has litigated immunity and accountability issues—including qualified immunity, judicial immunity, Bivens, and the Federal Tort Claims Act—across the United States and at every level of the American court system.

Four of Patrick’s cases have reached the U.S. Supreme Court. In November 2020, he argued the police brutality case Brownback v. King. Patrick returned to the Court in March of 2024 for the First Amendment retaliatory arrest case Gonzalez v. Trevino, which his colleague Anya Bidwell argued, and again in October 2024, when the Court granted, vacated, and reversed the denial of a similar retaliation claim in Murphy v. Schmitt. Most recently, Patrick argued the FBI wrong-house raid case Martin v. United States and secured a unanimous victory from the Supreme Court in June of 2025.

Before joining IJ, Patrick was a litigator at a private firm in Grand Rapids, Michigan, where he cultivated a civil rights practice and handled a variety of cases in state and federal court. He earned his law degree from the University of Chicago and a degree in economics and political science from the University of Notre Dame.

Patrick’s work has been featured in numerous publications, including the New York Times, Wall Street Journal, Washington Post, and USA Today. He has appeared on numerous podcasts and television and radio programs, authored several academic articles, and frequently gives presentations on his areas of expertise.

speakers.name: Ezra Chowaiki
speakers.bio:
Ezra Chowaiki has led his private art gallery, Chowaiki & Co., in New York City for over a decade. Founded in 2004, Chowaiki & Co. has established itself as a prominent gallery managing the acquisition and sale of art by Impressionist, Modern, Post-War and Contemporary masters. Ezra has helped his clientele build and refine their personal art collections through the variety of art advisory services the gallery offers. An authority in his field, he has exhibited works at art fairs across the United States and internationally, including The Armory Show in New York and Art Miami. Additionally, Ezra has shared his knowledge and expertise with a number of professional publications, such as Forbes, The New York Times, Art Info and Bloomberg.

Ezra Chowaiki is a graduate from New York University’s Tisch School of the arts with a bachelor of fine arts in comparative literature and film. Ezra furthered his expertise in 19th and 20th century art history through an intensive educational program at Sotheby’s.

speakers.name: Joanna Zelman
speakers.bio: Joanna Zelman is a Washington, DC-based filmmaker and consultant who tells stories about animals and the environment. Her short documentary Cow Trip has drawn more than 8 million views across the film and its short-form clips, and was featured by The Washington Post, CBS, and Good Morning America First Look. She previously served as editor of HuffPost Green, then spent ten years as Executive Producer of Vox Media’s The Dodo, the world’s #1 animal brand, where she helped grow the team to garner over 1 billion views per month. Additional producing credits include Dodo Heroes (Animal Planet), My Pack Life (Discovery+), and Rescued by Roman (Disney+).

speakers.name: Maggie Penman
speakers.bio: Maggie Penman is a reporter for The Optimist, writing surprising and hopeful stories about humanity. Previously she was the Executive Producer of “Post Reports,” The Washington Post’s award-winning flagship daily news podcast. She also reported and produced for NPR and its member stations, WGBH and WNYC. While at NPR, Penman helped launch the popular social science podcast “Hidden Brain,” contributed breaking news and features reporting to the network, and worked as a producer on Morning Edition.

speakers.name: Casey Mock
speakers.bio: Casey Mock is a nationally recognized voice on technology, democracy and the future of civic life, known for connecting big-picture research with practical insights for policymakers and communities. He serves as Senior Policy Advisor to social psychologist Jonathan Haidt and the national movement behind The Anxious Generation, focusing on how digital technologies shape youth well-being and democratic trust. He teaches courses in technology policy and the interplay between politics and innovation in Duke’s Science and Society program and writes Tomorrow’s Mess, a newsletter on how emerging technology is remaking politics, culture and governance. Over his career, Casey has served both Democratic and Republican governors, led the Vermont Economic Progress Council, advised Minnesota’s governor on budget and policy and worked on state and local public policy at Amazon.

speakers.name: Jenny Anderson
speakers.bio: Jenny Anderson an award-winning journalist, speaker, and author who studies how to help kids become successful learners. Against the backdrop of a youth mental health crisis and unprecedented rates of student disengagement, she offers parents and educators proven and practical interventions to build motivation, agency and resilience. Jenny has spent the past two decades on staff at major publications, including the New York Times and Quartz, reporting on education, the attention economy, learning science, technology, parenting, and innovation.

speakers.name: Crystal McCrary McGuire
speakers.bio:
Crystal McCrary McGuire began her career practicing entertainment law with the New York City firm Paul Weiss before leaving to pursue a full-time career in writing, producing, and directing. Since that time, she has published two New York Times Best Selling novels HOMECOURT ADVANTAGE and GOTHAM DIARIES and written the critically acclaimed non-fiction book INSPIRATION: Profiles of Black Women Changing the World. She also produced the independent film DIRTY LAUNDRY. For six seasons, Ms. McCrary served as executive producer for the NAACP Image Award nominated BET series LEADING WOMEN and LEADING MEN.

Additionally, Ms. McCrary directed six short films on the NAACP Legal Defense Fund. In 2022 she directed a short film about the life and career of Kenneth Frazier, former CEO of Merck. Most recently she co-founded Get To Yes, a full-service production company creating scripted and non-scripted content at the intersection of culture, sports and the socio-political landscape. Current Get To Yes projects include documentaries on the Olympian Allyson Felix, “The Drug in Our Pocket,” “Fatherless No More.” To commemorate Ariel Investments 40th Anniversary, she directed a documentary on the journey of John W. Rogers Jr. and Mellody Hobson in building the first Black-owned mutual fund firm in the country.

Ms. McCrary has appeared on numerous networks from CNN to MSNBC as a cultural, legal, and political pundit as well as co-hosted ABC’s The View. She currently sits on the Board the Paley Center for Media. Ms. McCrary has received numerous honors and distinctions including being honored by The Children’s Defense Fund, Precious Dreams Foundation, Children’s Museum of Manhattan, and Urban Tech for her contributions to youth and the arts. She was also named to Crain’s 40 under 40 Young Professionals list.

speakers.name: Beth Kojima
speakers.bio: Beth Kojima is a co-founder of GTY Productions, a full-service production company that brings together innovators in sports, fashion, finance, pop culture, politics, and the arts.  Beth began her career at Goldman Sachs, working in the Investment Management and Investment Banking Divisions.  Beth subsequently worked at a hedge fund, TPG-Axon Capital, as the Partner in charge of Investor Relations and Strategy.  Beth went on to Co-Found an ongoing education concept, Never Stop Learning (NSL), and subsequently worked on Ray McGuire’s mayoral campaign in New York City as the Director of Strategic Partnerships, running content for the campaign. Beth graduated from Duke University, magna cum laude, and received her MBA, beta gamma sigma, from Columbia Business School.  Beth serves as a Trustee of the New York Public Library, The Johns Hopkins Hospital, The Chapin School, and she serves on the Women’s Board of the Boys Club of New York (BCNY).  Beth also sits on the Board of Visitors for the Sanford School of Public Policy at Duke University, and is a member of the Dean’s Emeriti Circle for Trinity College at Duke University. Beth grew up in Baltimore, and currently lives in New York City with her husband and four children.

speakers.name: Jason Sussberg
speakers.bio: Jason Sussberg is a Bay-Area based documentary filmmaker and director at Structure Films, where he and his filmmaking partner David Alvarado specialize in Cinema for Science. Like Phil Ochs, he is a card carrying union member (Writers Guild of America), making art about our modern times. Unlike Ochs, he can’t carry a tune but instead carries a microphone. He has produced and directed several theatrical documentaries that have broadcast on PBS and streamed on Netflix, Apple TV, & Amazon. His titles include “The Immortalists” (2014), “Bill Nye: Science Guy” (2017), and “We Are As Gods” (2021). He has written and directed episodes for NOVA on PBS: “Your Brain: Who’s in Control?” (Season 50) and “Secrets in Your Data” (Season 51). Jason most recently wrote and produced the film trilogy “Matter of Mind” (2023-2025) on PBS’s Independent Lens. He and Alvarado are now directing the forthcoming “All Shall Be Saved” (2027), about the existential threats facing the Internet Archive. Jason grew up in Grass Valley California and lives in the Bay Area. He graduated from UC Santa Cruz (‘04) with a degree in Film & Digital Media, and earned an MFA from Stanford in Documentary Film. He was a producer/editor for the San Francisco Giants and Golden State Warriors from 2005-2008, working in his preferred medium: Jumbotron.

speakers.name: Bonnie Bertram
speakers.bio: Bonnie Bertram is Vice President of Content Development at Retro Report. She directed “Facing Eviction” for PBS Frontline and was Co-Executive Producer of the primetime series “Retro Report on PBS.” Her short film for The New York Times on vaccine hesitancy was nominated for a News and Documentary Emmy Award.

speakers.name: Christalyn Hampton
speakers.bio: Christalyn Hampton is an award-winning director and producer. Her achievements include “The Rebellious Life of Mrs. Rosa Parks,” (Peacock/Soledad O’Brien Productions) which earned her a Peabody, Gracie, and Television Academy Honors; the docuseries “Born in Synanon,” for Paramount+, a documentary “Rise and Rebuild: A Tale of Three Cities” (One Story Up and Tribeca Studios), and “Maxine Baby: The Tyler Perry Story” (Amazon Prime). Recently, she teamed with filmmaker Geeta Gandbhir to co-direct the Oscar-nominated “The Devil Is Busy,” a documentary short now streaming on HBO Max, and directed She Was First, a six-episode series for South Florida PBS.

speakers.name: Nichole Christian
speakers.bio: Nichole Christian is a writer, editor, and native Detroiter. She is currently the managing editor for Outlier Media, based in Detroit. Nichole has written extensively about the role artists play in cities’ cultural revitalization. She is the co-author of the award-winning public art book, Canvas Detroit. Previously, she worked as a staff writer for The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, Time magazine, and the Detroit Free Press. Her background also includes stints curating and moderating community engagement conversations for the former Freep Film Festival and arts nonprofits in the Midwest. Nichole is also a proud mom: One daughter, one dog.

speakers.name: Cheryl Fields
speakers.bio: Cheryl Fields leads Black Public Media’s marketing, communications and engagement team. During her tenure at BPM, the organization has dramatically increased its social media presence, broadened its individual donor base, and won one Peabody and five Anthem awards. Cheryl’s background in journalism and public relations informs her role leading the enhancement of BPM’s visibility in the media sector. A graduate of Bryn Mawr College, she holds a masters in journalism from the University of Southern California, is a former Poynter Institute Fellow, and a former NETA Public Media Diversity Fellow of Furman University’s Riley Institute.

speakers.name: Alana Rocha
speakers.bio: Alana Rocha is the director of collaborative and rural initiatives at the Institute for Nonprofit News, where she leads national strategy and partnerships to strengthen reporting in underserved communities. She oversees INN’s Rural News Network — one of the organization’s most ambitious collaborations — aligning more than 95 member newsrooms to expand and elevate coverage of rural America. Rocha joined INN following a 20-year career as a news and politics reporter across Florida, Kansas and Texas. Most recently, she worked at The Texas Tribune, where she directed news partnerships and led the production of award-winning multimedia journalism in English and Spanish.

speakers.name: Agnes Varnum
speakers.bio: Agnes Varnum bridges independent film and live journalism. Founder of Power the Press, she designs event strategies for newsrooms nationwide, including KUT, The Trace and Spotlight PA. She led 500-plus events at The Texas Tribune, including The Texas Tribune Festival, after a decade in documentary film as a program manager, event producer and writer.

speakers.name: Shannon Thomas
speakers.bio: Shannon Thomas joined Media Impact Funders from the Free Library of Philadelphia Foundation producing membership events and at the Science History Institute working across their award programs and lecture series. Prior to this, she worked for Doc Society in New York, first as an operations administrator and then, overseeing the Good Pitch Local program across the US. She holds an M.A in Arts Administration & Cultural Policy from Goldsmiths, University of London and a B.A. in Historical Studies from Bard College. When she’s not at work you can find her reading, chasing her dog around the house, and waking up too early on weekends to watch car racing.

speakers.name: Lynette Clemetson
speakers.bio:
Lynette Clemetson is the Charles R. Eisendrath Director of Wallace House, home of the Knight-Wallace Fellowships for Journalists and the Livingston Awards for Young Journalists at the University of Michigan. She is a 2010 Knight-Wallace alum and returned to the University of Michigan from NPR where she was Senior Director of Strategy and Content Initiatives, developing and guiding projects across broadcast, digital and events. Her career in journalism spans newspapers, magazines and audio across a range of platforms.

As a reporter, she was a Washington-based correspondent for The New York Times and Newsweek, writing about politics, social issues and demographic change. Prior to her domestic correspondent work, she was an international correspondent for Newsweek based in Hong Kong, where she covered the former British colony’s return to Chinese rule in 1997. She moved into digital strategy and leadership in 2008 as the founding managing editor of the website TheRoot.com, launched for The Washington Post Company with Henry Louis Gates Jr. She is also the former Director of Content Strategy at Pew Center on the States.

Lynette has a passionate interest in press freedom issues. She serves on the board of Forbidden Stories, an award-winning news organization dedicated to publishing the work of journalists who have been threatened, jailed or killed. Additionally, she is a member of the steering committee of the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press. She serves on the advisory boards for PBS FRONTLINE and the Knight-Press Freedom Fellowship at CUNY’s Craig Newark Graduate School of Journalism.

speakers.name: Nat Fernandez
speakers.bio: Nat Fernandez is an artist and digital storyteller working to deliver positive messages about community, personhood, and the natural world to diverse audiences.

speakers.name: Sherry Williams
speakers.bio: Sherry Williams is a creative event strategist who thrives where bold ideas meet complex logistics. With years of experience producing major conferences, high-profile gatherings, and curated experiences, she has built a reputation for turning ambitious concepts into seamless productions. Equal parts creative thinker and logistical problem-solver, Sherry brings vision, resourcefulness, and intention to every project, creating experiences that foster connection, cultivate community, and deliver meaningful impact.

speakers.name: Adam Mellion
speakers.bio: Adam Mellion is a Minneapolis-based researcher and fact-checker for documentaries and non-fiction books. His film credits include Laura Poitras’ Cover-Up (2025) and All the Beauty and the Bloodshed (2022), Musk (Alex Gibney, 2026), Who Moves America (Yael Bridge, 2026), Predators (David Osit, 2025), and Caterpillar (Liza Mandelup, 2023).

speakers.name: Bonnie Rowan
speakers.bio: With a graduate degree in film, Bonnie Rowan came from Wisconsin to work for the U.S. Information Agency but was soon teaching film studies and production as an Assistant Professor at Towson University in Baltimore. She wrote two books describing media resources in the Washington area. Then began an almost 40 year career as a professional on-site media researcher specializing in the vast and often rights-free collections of film and photos at the National Archives and Library of Congress. Rowan has research credits on over 500 productions including several Oscar and Emmy nominees. She was nominated for an Emmy in Research for RAPE OF EUROPA and MINE WARS. Past projects range from BETTY PAGE REVEALS ALL to AMERICAN REDS to SALINGER. Current projects include WWII in the Philippines and statehood for Washington DC.

speakers.name: Libby Liu
speakers.bio:
“Whistleblowers are our first line of defense when it comes to creating real and lasting change. After a lifetime of working with activists, journalists and freedom-fighters of many different kinds, I understand how vital it is to push back against corporations and governments and the tremendous power they are capable of wielding to discredit or silence truth-tellers. Whistleblower Aid is where I can put my fierce commitment to the truth into practice each and every day, and it is an honor to provide those with the courage to speak out with the resources and support they need to be heard loud and clear.”

Libby Liu is an internationally renowned expert on human rights, press freedom, information operations and internet freedom who joined Whistleblower Aid as chief executive officer in April 2021.

Prior to joining Whistleblower Aid, Ms. Liu created the Open Technology Fund (OTF), where she spearheaded efforts to support tools that circumvent censorship and surveillance and advance free speech worldwide. Today, more than 2 billion people use OTF-supported technologies every day, including Signal, TOR and Wireguard.

Ms. Liu was compelled to create OTF to protect the digital lives of individuals while serving as president of Radio Free Asia (RFA), a non-profit media company that provides uncensored objective news and information otherwise unavailable to audiences in East Asia. In 16 years at the helm, she led RFA’s vision, directed RFA’s editorial strategy and shaped its administrative policies, working closely with a bipartisan board, its grantor agency, USAGM, oversight and appropriations committees of the U.S. Congress, the State Department, international public broadcasters and stakeholders in the U.S. and abroad.

Ms. Liu has served as assistant district attorney in the San Francisco District Attorney’s office and is a former corporate labor and employment law attorney.

She holds a bachelor’s degree from the University of California-Berkeley, an MBA from The Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania, and a J.D. from the University of Pennsylvania Law School. In 2021, she was honored as a Luxembourg Peace Prize laureate for outstanding work on technology that promotes peace.

speakers.name: Alexandra Genova
speakers.bio:
Alexandra Genova is a BAFTA-winning documentary director, journalist and creative producer based in London. Her work spans documentary film, broadcast television and digital media, creating visually led stories about culture, identity and social justice.

Her films have been commissioned by organisations including the BBC, Sky Documentaries, ITV, Together TV and TIME. Her short documentary Our Land won a BAFTA in the Short Form category in 2022 and screened at several BAFTA-qualifying film festivals. She also directed the BFI-funded documentary The Keeper (2023), which follows a Scottish landowner attempting to challenge concentrated land ownership from within.

She is currently directing Casa Mia, a documentary exploring the lives of women connected to the Neapolitan Camorra.

Alongside her filmmaking, Alexandra works as a journalist and has written for publications including The Guardian, The New York Times, TIME, National Geographic, The Economist and Al Jazeera. A trained magazine journalist with over a decade of experience, she specialises in long-form storytelling and character-driven reporting.

As a creative producer, she has also worked across agency and client-facing projects, including global video campaigns for brands such as Airbnb and Adidas, and editorial collaborations at Magnum Photos and TIME.

Alexandra is of Native American, Italian and Welsh descent. She was born in New York City and raised in England, and holds dual US and UK citizenship. She has a Master’s degree in Magazine Journalism from City University London.

speakers.name: Maia Wikler
speakers.bio: Maia Wikler is a Ph.D. candidate in political ecology, a writer, and a filmmaker, based on Vancouver Island, BC, Canada. A recipient of the Lorene Kennedy Environmental Scholarship, her research focuses on memory as a tool of resistance in the face of corporate abuse, specifically deforestation. Her reporting appears in Teen Vogue, VICE, Vogue, High Country News, and Canada’s National Observer, among many others. She was awarded the CC Faces of Innovation for her work at the UN Climate Talks in Germany. As a member of The North Face Explorers Arctic Expedition, Wikler reported on the unfolding climate crisis for Teen Vogue. Her reporting was presented to congressional leaders on Capitol Hill. She furthered her advocacy efforts for the Arctic Refuge as the director, writer, and producer of the documentary film, Walking Two Worlds, which premiered at the Tribeca Film Festival. As a National Geographic Explorer, her work documented cross-border salmon stories and the threats to wild salmon from mining in Northern British Columbia. Wikler was recently selected as a filmmaker-in-residence at the Woodstock Film Festival, where she worked on her documentary short, Wild East, set to premiere in the winter of 2026.

speakers.name: Marie-Josée Desharnais
speakers.bio:
Marie-Josée (MJ) Desharnais is a Filipina-Québécoise documentary filmmaker, writer, and interdisciplinary artist based in Montréal. Her practice moves between experimental documentary, sound, archives, and embodied forms of storytelling, exploring memory, dissociation, adoption, diasporic identity, and survival.

Her experimental short SURRENDERED (2025) has received 23 selections, screenings, and programming invitations since beginning its circulation in May 2026, reaching audiences through artist-run cine-clubs, underground screenings, independent showcases, and international film festivals across North and South America and Europe, with its African premiere forthcoming in Cape Town, South Africa.

The film received two nominations at the 2026 Atlanta Experimental Fest for Best Experimental Documentary and the Experimental Vision Award and a third nomination for Best Experimental Short Film at the Cuzco Underground Cinema Festival in Peru, where it went on to win the award. SURRENDERED was also selected for Labocine’s international curatorial archive, Science New Wave.

She is currently developing her first feature-length documentary, Weaving Identity. Rooted in her personal exploration of identity, memory, and belonging, the hybrid project opens onto a collective dimension, weaving together fragmented archives, voices, gestures, sound, and material practices to explore how identities are shaped, negotiated, and shared across generations, communities, and diasporic experiences between Canada and the Philippines.

speakers.name: Arjun Fischer
speakers.bio: Arjun Fischer is an documentary director and editor from Oakton, Virginia. He has been nominated for three Emmys and two Producers Guild Awards for his work as a producer and editor of non-fiction television. He worked at NFL Films and Warner Bros before pursuing his MFA, and his work can be seen on HBO Max, Netflix, Paramount+, and more. His short doucumentary directorial debut won the 2026 Student Academy Award. He loves telling character studies through documentary while interrogating uncomfortable and scary topics with a curious lens.

speakers.name: Anne Sundberg
speakers.bio:
Anne Sundberg is known for creating critically acclaimed films and television series. Her work has been shortlisted for the Oscars, won a Columbia-Dupont Silver Baton and earned 13 Emmy and 2 Peabody nominations and numerous festival accolades. Her films include: My So-Called High School Rank (HBO); Reversing Roe (Netflix); Marathon: The Patriots Day Bombing (HBO); In My Father’s House (Showtime); Knuckleball!; Burma Soldier (HBO); The Bengali Detective (IHBO); Joan Rivers – A Piece of Work; The Devil Came on Horseback and The Trials of Darryl Hunt. Additional films include the Oscar winning One Survivor Remembers (HBO) and the narrative feature Tully. 

She is a member of the Academy of Motion Pictures Arts and Sciences, the DGA and the Television Academy, and lives in New York City with her husband and daughter.

speakers.name: Annukka Lilja
speakers.bio: Annukka Lilja is a Finnish-born, New York-based film editor whose award-winning films have appeared on HBO, Netflix, PBS and at major film festivals worldwide – including Sundance, Tribeca, SXSW and IDFA. Her recent documentary editing work includes The Inquisitor (Tribeca 2025), Peabody Award winning HBO series Stax: Soulsville USA (SXSW 2024), Ailey, (Sundance 2021), Mr. SOUL! (2020 Critics Choice Award winner, Tribeca 2021), Bill Nye: Science Guy (SXSW 2017). Annukka won the Best Editing Award at the United Nations Association Film Festival (UNAFF 2016) for How to Let Go of the World (Sundance 2016).

speakers.name: Steven Leckart
speakers.bio: Steven Leckart is an Emmy-winning filmmaker and investigative journalist. In 2025, he wrote and directed STANS, the feature documentary about Eminem that received a worldwide theatrical release and premiered on Paramount+. His directorial debut was CHALLENGER: THE FINAL FLIGHT, a four-part Netflix documentary series he co-directed and produced with Bad Robot that received two News & Documentary Emmy nominations. He also wrote and executive produced the Emmy-winning LEGACY: THE TRUE STORY OF THE LA LAKERS (Hulu) and wrote the Emmy-winning WHAT’S MY NAME | MUHAMMAD ALI (HBO). His writing has appeared in WIRED, The New York Times Magazine, Popular Science, and Esquire. In 2020, his investigative feature “The Bicycle Thief” was selected for The Best American Sports Writing and was a finalist at the National City and Regional Magazine Awards.

speakers.name: Miriam Shor
speakers.bio: Miriam Shor has worked as a director and actor in the film and television industry for over 25 years, and has focused on stories and characters that challenge traditional female narratives. She was recently nominated for an Emmy for her portrayal of HELEN in the AppleTV’s television show Pluribus. She directed and starred in the critically acclaimed television show YOUNGER on Paramount+/Netflix, earning a Critics Choice nomination for her work. She collaborated with director/actor John Cameron Mitchell on both the original off-Broadway production of HEDWIG AND THE ANGRY INCH as well as the subsequent groundbreaking feature film, creating the iconic role of “Yitzak”, (LA Outfest Award, Phoenix Critics Circle nom., Satellite Award nom.) Her work can be seen on AppleTV, HBO, FX, Netflix, ABC, CBS, NBC and many other platforms. Miriam is a proud union member of the Directors Guild of America, SAG-AFTRA and AEA.

speakers.name: William Segal
speakers.bio: William Segal wrote the music and lyrics of Rhapsody on the Outlaw Ocean. Also, as the project’s co-executive producer, he recruited and led the project’s seventeen performers, animators, and musical producers. A classically trained musician with undergraduate and graduate degrees from Stanford University, he has been working since 2006 at the intersection of rap and musical theater. His rap opera Outflow, inspired by New Orleans and Hurricane Katrina, was performed at Stanford. His musical Superhero Celebrity Rehab received a number of workshops and full productions spanning 2009-2019 in New York and Washington, DC, including a Best Musical win at the Capitol Fringe Festival in 2012. After Segal met Ian Urbina in 2017, Rhapsody on the Outlaw Ocean began as an idea for a five-song EP and grew gradually to its current incarnation as an hourlong fully animated film. In his work as a composer, and also as an educator, Segal is drawn to exploring new ways that language and insight can make unmanageable problems more manageable.

speakers.name: Andreas Dalsgaard
speakers.bio: Andreas Dalsgaard is an independent director and producer and founder of Danish doc production house Elk Film. His most recent directing and writing credits include Venice Days winner The War Show, which took home the Venice Days Award, the hit documentary The Lost Leonardo, the AFI winner Afghan Muscles and Al Jazeera Grand Prix winner The Human Scale. His most recent producing credits include Hacking Hate, As the Tide Comes In and Daughter of Genghis.

speakers.name: Christoph Jörg
speakers.bio:
Christoph Jörg is an independent documentary producer and Story Consultant with thirty years of experience. As the founder of Paris-based Vestigo Films (2022) and Pumpernickel Films (2009), and the Managing Director of Unchained Productions in New York, his recent works, include:

An Eye for an Eye, The Oligarch and the Art Dealer, The Lost Leonardo, One Child Nation, Winnie, The Lovers and the Despot, Love Crimes of Kabul, Be Like Others, and As Far as They Can Run.

Christoph worked as Senior Commissioning Editor for Arte France in Paris from 1992 to 2009, where he oversaw the conception and production of more than 300 documentaries. He is a member of the Producers Guild of America (PGA) and lives in New York.

speakers.name: Andrew H. Brown
speakers.bio:
Andrew H. Brown (Huron-Wendat/Scottish) is an Emmy Award winning filmmaker and storyteller that was born & raised in Alaska. He has spent the past decade living and working across sub-Saharan Africa, first as a humanitarian, then behind the camera. Andrew’s work centers on intimate, long-form documentary projects that amplify often unheard voices and tackle the deep complexities of land, identity, and power.

Andrew is the director, cinematographer, producer, and editor of KIKUYU LAND (Sundance Festival 2026 World Cinema Documentary competition), an investigative feature documentary examining historical land injustices and present-day corporate power in Kenya’s tea highlands. The film builds on years of on-the-ground reporting and close collaboration with Kenyan partners and communities.

Previously, Andrew was the director, cinematographer, producer, and editor of BETWEEN THE RAINS (Tribeca 2023 Grand Jury Prize for Best Documentary Feature and Best Cinematography; IDA Award nominee for Best Cinematography; Cinema Eye Honors nominee for Best Production). He was also editor of National Geographic’s Emmy-winning PATH OF THE PANTHER (executive produced by Leonardo DiCaprio), a bold meditation on conservation in the Florida Everglades.

Earlier, Andrew produced, shot, and edited KIFARU (Audience Award, Full Frame 2019), a deeply personal look at the final years of the world’s last male northern white rhino and the small team of Kenyan caretakers who lived with him, earning a Jackson Wild nomination for Best Editing. His work also includes WHEN LAMBS BECOME LIONS (Tribeca 2018 winner for Best Editing), a vérité portrait of the ivory trade in northern Kenya developed over three years of trust-based access within poaching networks. Most recently, Andrew was a shooter for THE LAST RHINOS: A NEW HOPE (National Geographic / Disney+).

A 2022 Points North Fellow, Andrew brings a distinct creative vision and strong editorial sensitivity to every story he tells, often working across roles to carry projects from field production through final cut.

speakers.name: Bea Wangondu
speakers.bio: Bea Wangondu is an award-winning producer, journalist and founder of The Bea Company, a Kenya-based creative studio dedicated to high quality and culturally rich storytelling with a strong focus on women and girls. Her work spans documentaries, branded films and community-centered narratives designed for global audiences. Wangondu is the co-director of Kikuyu Land, alongside Andrew H. Brown. Most recently, Bea was a producer for The Last Rhinos: A New Hope (National Geographic). Her short Supastarz made its international premiere at the Durban International Film Festival in 2022 and was nominated at the Zanzibar International Film Festival (ZIFF). Additional credits include Netflix’s Kipchoge: The Last Milestone, the award-winning film The Whistleblower, Wariyaha and Rastasophical Moods.

speakers.name: Sine Plambech
speakers.bio: Sine Plambech is an anthropologist and award-winning film director of Heartbound (World premier at TIFF 2018) with Janus Metz, Love on Delivery (2008) with Janus Metz, Ticket to Paradise (2008) with Janus Metz, Trafficking (2010) with Judith Lansade and Becky’s Journey (2014). She documents international migration, sex work and human trafficking. Based in Copenhagen and New York she is a Senior Researcher at the Danish Institute for International Studies (DIIS).

speakers.name: Elina Hirvonen
speakers.bio: Elina Hirvonen is an award-winning Finnish documentary filmmaker and author whose work has been recognized internationally. Her first feature Paradise: Three Journeys in This World won the main prize for student films at IDFA 2007. Boiling Point, 2017, was named Best Documentary at the Lübeck Nordisk Film Days and Uruguay’s Tenemos Que Ver festival. She has recently been awarded the WSOY Foundation Recognition Award for artistic achievement (2023), the Finnish Red Cross Human Reach Award (2024) and both the Finnish PEN and International Press Institute Finland awards for her contributions to freedom of expression.

speakers.name: Shakiba Adil
speakers.bio: Shakiba Adil is a documentary filmmaker, journalist, educator, and women’s rights activist born and raised in Kabul and living in Finland. She grew up under the first Taliban regime and, after its fall in 2001, became the first woman to appear on Afghan television as well as one of the country’s first female documentary filmmakers. Her film, Afghanistan Unveiled (2002), co-directed with an Afghan-French team, was nominated for an Emmy in 2004. Adil has directed documentaries for, among others, the Finnish broadcasting company Yle, combining lived experience and inside knowledge of Afghanistan with an uncompromising artistic voice.

speakers.name: Pegah Ahangarani
speakers.bio: Pegah Ahangarani is a prominent Iranian filmmaker and actress with a career spanning over three decades. Following her breakthrough performance in The Girl in the Sneakers (1999) and a filmography of over 40 feature films, Ahangarani expanded her practice into documentary filmmaking alongside her acting. Her directorial work includes the essay documentaries I Am Trying to Remember (2021) and My Father (2023), as well as Child Soldier (2024) and Taraneh (2025). Her films have received critical acclaim and garnered prestigious awards at international festivals including IDFA and Busan.

speakers.name: Galassia Grassetto
speakers.bio:
Galassia Grassetto is the director, producer, and editor of The Sludge War, a five-year investigation into a secretive government program that has endangered the health and homes of millions of Americans for more than half a century.

Her work is driven by stories in which the accepted version of events begins to fall apart under scrutiny, particularly when powerful institutions shape the narrative and the people living with the consequences struggle to be heard. She is drawn to investigations that demand persistence, independence, and a willingness to keep asking questions.

That instinct developed early. Grassetto began diving with sharks at a young age and discovered they were far from the monsters she had been taught to believe. The experience deepened a lasting passion for wildlife and environmental issues.

Raised between France, Mexico, and Italy and fluent in four languages, Galassia grew up immersed in different cultures and perspectives.

speakers.name: Marisa Fox
speakers.bio: Marisa Fox is a veteran journalist and a first-time, awrd-winning film director who has been a producer at FX, Channel 13-WNET (NYC’s PBS station), Vh1 and MTV. As a correspondent for Haaretz, Newsday, New York and a contributor to The Daily Beast, Rolling Stone, CNN, Forward and The New York Times, she has reported on major news stories from 9/11 to the opioid crisis, from Charlottesville to January 6th to October 7th. She’s a “she-source” on gender and genocide for the Women’s Media Center, founded by Gloria Steinem and Robin Morgan,  was deputy editor at Billboard and InStyle, helped relaunch The Hollywood Reporter, and worked on award-winning digital features for Hearst, where she served as entertainment director and wrote cover stories. Fox’s more than 10-year global search to uncover her late mother’s hidden past led her to curate one of the only women’s Holocaust monuments, at the former Gabersdorf Jewish women’s forced labor camp, as well as a digital exhibit of women’s testimonies with USC’s Shoah Foundation. Fox is a 2022 Jewish Film Institute resident, won Pitch Royale at the Australian International Screen Forum and was a finalist at Paley Doc Pitch. She cut her teeth in investigative journalism as a college intern at Chicago’s Better Government Association and covered foreign affairs as an intern for the Jerusalem Post’s Washington, DC bureau. She holds an MS and BS in Journalism and a BA in French Language & Literature from Northwestern University, earning a National Magazine Award for her master’s thesis publication Arts Chicago. She is currently writing a book about her search for her mother’s missing past.

speakers.name: Jarrett Ley
speakers.bio: Jarrett Ley is a visual forensics reporter at The Washington Post. His reporting mobilizes open-source investigation methods alongside spatial analysis techniques honed through his prior training in architecture. His reporting was featured in the Post’s 2024 Pulitzer Prize-winning coverage of the attempted assassination of Donald Trump.

speakers.name: Swapneel Mehta
speakers.bio:
Dr. Swapneel Mehta is a former postdoc in AI safety at MIT and worked on elections integrity at Twitter. He co-founded and serves as the president of the nonprofit SimPPL which recently launched an AI platform, Arbiter, to help prevent the manipulation of public views on health, elections, democracy, and policy.

SimPPL works with national newsrooms, fact-checkers, and a few govt. agencies across 23 countries. The organization can now show you what shapes your feed before it ends up shaping your views. SimPPL’s work has received awards from MIT, Google, Wikimedia, Mozilla, and were recently profiled in Nieman Lab.

speakers.name: Will Thwaites
speakers.bio: Will Thwaites is a documentary filmmaker based in Brooklyn, New York. He’s worked on projects for Netflix, Amazon, Hulu, and PBS. Will was a producer on two acclaimed Netflix series: Full Swing and My Next Guest with David Letterman. He started his career at Kartemquin Films (Oscar-nominated producers of Minding the Gap and Hoop Dreams), where he worked on the Emmy Award-winning film, The Homestretch. Will’s debut feature documentary, Crime & Parody, premiered at Big Sky Documentary Film Festival in 2026, won best documentary feature at the River Valley Film Festival, and is playing at film festivals across the country.

speakers.name: James McLaughlin
speakers.bio: James McLaughlin is deputy general counsel of The Washington Post, where he is principally responsible for newsroom-related legal issues and litigation, including libel, privacy, the First Amendment, subpoenas, FOIA, access to judicial proceedings, and intellectual property. Since 2015, he also oversees the Post’s participation in legislative and lobbying activities as its director of government affairs. Before joining the Post in 2006, he was an associate at Covington & Burling (1999-2003) and Zuckerman Spaeder (2004-06), and the McCormick Tribune Legal Fellow at The Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press (2003-04). He is a graduate of Amherst College and Yale Law School (Senior Editor, The Yale Law Journal), and a former law clerk to the Honorable Anthony J. Scirica of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit.

speakers.name: Juliane Dressner
speakers.bio: Juliane Dressner is a director, producer, cinematographer and editor whose observational documentaries explore civil rights and other pressing societal issues. Her feature-length debut, PERSONAL STATEMENT, premiered as the opening night film at AFI DOCS, was broadcast on PBS and was nominated for an Emmy Award. Juliane directed, produced and shot PERSONAL STATEMENT and her second feature, My NDA, which premiered at SXSW and is currently screening in festivals throughout the world. Juliane’s other films include THE SCARS OF STOP-AND-FRISK, a documentary short that was part of an Emmy-winning season of the Op-Docs series from The New York Times. She won the National Magazine Award for Video for her short film, AN EDUCATION, which was published by The New York Times Magazine. She has also had films published by The Guardian, The Atlantic, New York magazine and Buzzfeed. Her third feature-length documentary, EDUCATING ELIZABETH, is supported by Latino Public Broadcasting and will be completed in 2027.

speakers.name: Ashley Kostial
speakers.bio: After making the bold decision to speak out against her NDA, Ashley Kostial has focused her efforts on turning her personal experience with workplace assault and corporate intimidation into advocacy for those who find themselves in similar circumstances. Ashley has shared her story in various publications including Business Insider, Bloomberg News and The Wall Street Journal. Ashley’s story is also featured in the recently released documentary film My NDA. She plans to expand her advocacy leveraging this platform.

speakers.name: Doug Block
speakers.bio:
Doug Block is a New York-based documentary director-producer and highly sought-after story consultant. His critically acclaimed, multiple award-winning feature films — including 51 BIRCH STREET, THE KIDS GROW UP, and 112 WEDDINGS — have screened at dozens of leading international film festivals and have been released theatrically and broadcast on television throughout the world.

His popular Substack newsletter, “Getting Personal with Doug Block,” focuses on personal documentary filmmaking, first-person storytelling, and producing for film. In addition, Doug is the founder and co-host of The D-Word, the leading online discussion forum and community for documentary filmmakers worldwide. He currently serves on the Advisory Board of the Full Frame Documentary Film Festival and is a member of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences.

speakers.name: Lisa Warwick
speakers.bio:
Lisa Warwick is the Manager of The People’s Archive at DC Public Library. Warwick has been instrumental in enhancing reference services and access to the archive. In her role as Manager, she oversees a staff of eleven; caring for DC Public Library’s special collections, including the Black Studies; Washingtoniana; DC Punk Archive; Go-Go Archive; and Peabody Room Collections. A small sample of the collections can be seen online in our recently updated online repository, Dig DC. Previously, as a Coordinator, Warwick created (and adjusted) reference workflows in 2020, during the complex move across multiple locations into the newly renovated Martin Luther King, Jr. Memorial Library. She also developed a comprehensive department manual and implemented virtual reference options; including collaborating across the library system to establish a department-wide LibAnswers reference queue.

Earlier in her career, Warwick worked in academic and specialty research libraries, including the University of Maryland and Dumbarton Oaks Research Library, before coming to the DC Public Library in 2013. She holds her M.A. in Information Science from the University of Maryland and a B.A. in Film Studies from the University of Pittsburgh. Outside of work, she enjoys cooking, biking, and reading at home with her cat, Bruce.

speakers.name: Sasha Schell
speakers.bio: Sasha Schell is a documentary filmmaker and open-source investigative journalist from Berkeley, CA. As the Supervising Reporter at the Berkeley Human Rights Center, he reports outcomes from HRC’s investigations and supports student research. As a filmmaker, he has investigated how global supply chains for beef and palm oil have fueled violent land conflicts in the Brazilian Amazon. His most recent work examines the use of less lethal weapons against civilians in protests in the US. Before coming to Berkeley, Sasha was an associate producer and archival researcher for PBS FRONTLINE covering the conflicts in Syria and Afghanistan.

speakers.name: Yvonne Ng
speakers.bio: Yvonne Ng is an audiovisual archivist and Senior Manager of Training and Partnerships at WITNESS, a global organization that helps people use video to document the truth and defend human rights. She serves on the steering committee of the Trust in Archives Initiative (TAI), a coalition dedicated to preserving the authenticity of media collections, encouraging transparency, and ensuring public trust in archives. Yvonne holds an M.A in Moving Image Archiving and Preservation from New York University, and was the 2024 recipient of the Alan Stark Award from the Association of Moving Image Archivists in recognition of her contributions to moving image archives and the association.

speakers.name: Lois Nembhard
speakers.bio: Lois Nembhard is the Director of Community Engagement and Programs at DC History Center + HumanitiesDC. She leads the team that provides DC residents with resources to interpret, share, and celebrate the history, culture and stories that make up DC. DC residents can receive grants and fellowships, produce and attend public humanities programs, and learn about oral history and community journalism. Lois has spent much of her career in grantmaking and program management, including with AmeriCorps and the Social Innovation Fund. She received her bachelor’s degree from Mills College in California, and her master’s from the University of Pittsburgh Graduate School for Public and International Affairs.

speakers.name: Jeremiah Schofield
speakers.bio:
Jeremiah Schofield is a senior executive with more than 25 years of experience leading enterprise operations, organizational modernization, and workforce development across federal government, local government, and nonprofit sectors. He currently serves as Chief Administrative Officer for HELP USA, where he oversees Information Technology, Human Resources, Procurement, and Realty & Leasing for one of the nation’s largest human services nonprofits, supporting more than 1,300 employees, 70+ programs and sites, and 1,000+ vendor relationships.

Prior to HELP USA, Jeremiah held multiple Senior Executive Service roles at the Social Security Administration, where he led nationwide operations, digital modernization, and service delivery initiatives supporting more than 80 million customers annually. His federal career included oversight of multi-billion-dollar budgets, large-scale automation programs, and fraud prevention efforts that recovered hundreds of millions of dollars for taxpayers.

In 2026, Jeremiah became a whistleblower after filing a legal disclosure to Congress detailing a plan he witnessed within the Social Security Administration to misuse the agency’s death records for immigration enforcement purposes. His disclosure prompted a congressional investigation led by Senators Elizabeth Warren and Richard Blumenthal and drew national media attention.

An executive coach and elected local official, Jeremiah has coached more than 100 leaders across government, nonprofit, and private-sector organizations. He holds an MBA from City University of Seattle, executive education credentials from Harvard Kennedy School, and a coaching certification from the College of Executive Coaching.

speakers.name: Sonam Vashi
speakers.bio: Sonam Vashi is the director of the Documenters Network and program at City Bureau. The Documenters Network includes 20+ local organizations that equip and pay community members to attend local government meetings, distill what matters, and bring actionable information back to their neighbors. Our goal is to support communities to understand and shape the decisions that impact their lives and neighborhoods. Together, the network has trained more than 6,000 residents, documented more than 14,000 local meetings, and paid out more than $1.5 million directly to communities across the country. The program was founded and is supported nationally by City Bureau, a civic media lab designing and helping local adoption of people-powered journalism practices. Previously, Sonam cofounded Canopy Atlanta, a local community journalism nonprofit; was a 2022 John S. Knight Community Impact Fellow; and was an award-winning freelance investigative reporter for outlets including ProPublica, Atlanta magazine, CNN, and more. She lives in beautiful Atlanta, Georgia, where she was raised, with her two cats.

speakers.name: Matt Drange
speakers.bio: Matt Drange is an investigative reporter at the Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project (OCCRP). He previously reported for Business Insider, Forbes magazine and the Center for Investigative Reporting, among others. Matt’s reporting on educator sexual misconduct prompted the passage of a 2025 California law to better protect students, as well as numerous resignations, civil lawsuits, and criminal probes. His reporting on nondisclosure agreements in the tech industry, meanwhile, spurred corporate and regulatory change, and served as a springboard for the documentary, My NDA. Matt has often focused on issues revolving around money and power, with his stories sparking Congressional inquiries, state investigations, and dropped contracts by local governments. With a colleague, he broke the story in 2016 that billionaire investor Peter Thiel had secretly bankrolled a crippling invasion of privacy lawsuit against Gawker Media. Matt’s work has been recognized with numerous awards and accolades, including a Free Speech & Open Government Award from the First Amendment Coalition, a Sidney Award from the Hillman Foundation and multiple Best in Business awards from the Society for Advancing Business Editing & Writing (SABEW). In 2019, he was named by SABEW as the “Best Young Business Journalist” in the United States, and in 2024 was a finalist for the Livingston Award for National Reporting. Matt sits on SABEW’s First Amendment Committee and is a longtime member of Investigative Reporters and Editors (IRE). He graduated from Humboldt State University and holds a master’s degree from the Columbia Journalism School. Matt teaches investigative reporting at Laney College in Oakland, California.

speakers.name: Sam Benstead
speakers.bio: Sam Benstead is a filmmaker acclaimed for bringing warmth, big picture visuals and cinematic flair to the most difficult subjects. His work includes the hit Netflix series The Puppetmaster, which led to the arrest of conman Robert Freegard after its release; and award-winning Mumbai High, the first Bollywood musical documentary ever made. He was Director of Photography on Bobi Wine: The People’s President, which premiered at the Venice Film Festival before being nominated for an Oscar.

speakers.name: George Kevin Jordan
speakers.bio: George Kevin Jordan is a writer, author, illustrator, and visual artist whose work explores community, place, identity, and the outdoors. He serves as a Community Connector with The 51st, engaging Ward 7 residents in shaping local journalism, and as Lead Trainer for HumanitiesDC’s Community Journalism Program. His creative work spans journalism, fiction, essays, illustration, and visual art.

speakers.name: Noah Kincade
speakers.bio: Noah Kincade coordinates the Detroit Documenters program for Outlier Media, a hyperlocal, mission-driven newsroom serving the information needs of Detroiters. As a part of the larger Documenters Network created by Chicago journalism lab City Bureau, residents are trained and paid to attend and document local public meetings through written notes, multimedia recordings and live social media coverage. As coordinator, Noah teaches Detroiters how to watchdog their local government by documenting meetings that might otherwise go unreported. Before joining Outlier, Noah pursued a career in music and event production, leaving his home state of Michigan to plant roots in San Francisco, California. There, he developed his skills as a live sound engineer and eventually partnered with a few friends to operate an all-ages concert venue in the heart of the city. While in San Francisco, Noah spent several years pursuing tenant claims against a negligent landlord. That experience and time spent interacting with the city’s rent board reinforced his belief that local authorities can have direct and meaningful impact on people’s lives. Noah moved to Detroit’s eastside in 2020 with his partner and their two feline boys. Through his work with Outlier Media and the Documenters Network, Noah seeks to strengthen civic engagement by equipping Detroiters with the tools they need to improve their lives and hold power to account.

speakers.name: Amelia O’Rourke-Owens
speakers.bio: Amelia O’Rourke-Owens received her Juris Doctor summa cum laude from North Carolina Central University. She’s worked in community economic development, consumer protection, and programmatic implementation. The unifying thread in Amelia’s career is maximizing impact with minimal resources. She has built statewide systems, moved federal policy portfolios, and published two law review articles. Amelia spends her time consulting with nonprofits, institutions, and organizations that want to meet the moment.

speakers.name: Mark Graham
speakers.bio: Mark Graham is director of the Wayback Machine at the Internet Archive, where he works to make the Web more useful and reliable, archiving and making available hundreds of millions of Web pages a day — more than 1 trillion to date. Previously, Mark was senior vice president at NBC News Digital, managing business units including Stringwire, a live mobile video platform for collaborative citizen reporting. He was senior vice president of technology at iVillage: The Women’s Network, and cofounded Rojo Networks, one of the first large-scale feed aggregators and personalized blog readers. In the early days of the internet he led The WELL’s effort to build the first web-based interface for online forums, and brought the pre-web internet to millions by creating and running AOL’s Internet Center. He managed technology for the pioneering US-Soviet Sovam Teleport email service, and cofounded and led PeaceNet, one of the first online communities for progressive social change, and later the Institute for Global Communications, among the world’s first ISPs. He also cofounded the global NGO Association for Progressive Communications. Mark was introduced to computer-mediated communications in the U.S. Air Force, spending more than three years at the Air Force Data Services Center at the Pentagon. While still in uniform, he cofounded the Washington DC Campaign for a Nuclear Weapons Freeze, and later compiled a list of peace groups published as the Peace Resource Book while helping run a nationwide PR and organizing campaign for the movie The Day After.

speakers.name: Rachel Mason
speakers.bio: Rachel Mason is an award-winning Los Angeles based filmmaker. She received an Emmy nomination for the Netflix original documentary Circus of Books, which told the story her parents’ adult bookstore that served the gay community during the height of the AIDS crisis. In 2025, Mason directed the HBO Max series An Update on Our Family, which has since been cited in legal arguments advocating for changes to legislation aimed at protecting children’s privacy. In 2025, Hulu released Last Take: Rust and the Story of Halyna, a documentary about the death of her friend Halyna Hutchins on the set of the film Rust. In 2026, Mason completed My Brother’s Killer, about the 1990 murder of a young gay man which remained cold for 33 years until the film catalyzed the solving of the murder. The film and the crime solving was made entirely independently through a volunteer-driven community effort.

speakers.name: Shamara Mambazo
speakers.bio:
With seven years of experience in the hospitality and entertainment industry, Shamara currently serves as a Theatre Manager with the National Film Festival. Throughout their career, they have gained diverse leadership experience across theatres, bars, and hotels, developing a well-rounded understanding of both operations and guest experience.

Beginning their career as a coordinator, Shamara progressed into management within just three years—a reflection of their dedication, adaptability, and passion for leadership. Their supportive, team-driven leadership style centers on empowering others, building strong relationships, and creating an environment where both team members and guests can thrive.

At the heart of their work is a passion for creating exceptional experiences. Whether leading a team, managing operations, or welcoming guests, Shamara believes that the details matter and that great experiences are created through great people.

Outside of work, Shamara loves hosting dinner parties and cooking for their “village”—bringing people together through good food, great conversation, and a sense of community.

speakers.name: Sam Schwartz
speakers.bio: Sam Schwartz is a part of the class of 2028 in the College of Arts and Sciences at Georgetown University. He is studying Justice and Peace Studies and Film and Media Studies and hails from Boston, Massachusetts. Sam is involved with Georgetown’s Radio, their annual high school Model UN conference, and Jewish life on campus, having previously been employed by their Office of Jewish Life. He is also a part of Georgetown Sketch Comedy where he writes and performs in monthly sketch comedy shows. Outside of school he enjoys running and teaches at a Hebrew School.

speakers.name: Catherine Hughes
speakers.bio: Catherine Hughes is a rising senior at Georgetown University majoring in International Politics and minoring in Theater and Performance Studies. On campus, she is involved in performing arts and journalism, having been President of her a cappella group and Executive Director of GU Politics’ publication On The Record. Outside of school, she has participated in multiple film festivals, acting as an actor, makeup artist, casting director, and camera assistant for various short films. She is looking forward to bringing her experience in film and journalism to the team behind such an exciting festival.

speakers.name: Jodi Sakol
speakers.bio: Jodi Sakol is a Washington, DC–based documentary filmmaker. Her documentary follows a survivor of sex trafficking as she navigates recovery while building a nonprofit for women in crisis. She currently serves as the director of outreach for the Double Exposure Investigative Film Festival, managing sponsorships and public outreach. Previously, she served as the sponsorship and seminar coordinator for the DC Independent Film Festival, managing partnerships and supporting industry programming. She has served as a film screener for multiple festivals, reviewing submissions and identifying compelling independent work. Earlier in her career, she directed external outreach for U.S. Senate leadership, worked on numerous congressional campaigns, and served as the communications director for a Vice Presidential candidate.

speakers.name: Charles Poe
speakers.bio: Charles Poe is an Emmy- and Peabody-winning filmmaker and media executive whose work has appeared on National Geographic, Smithsonian and Discovery. Poe served as Executive Producer for the landmark series National Geographic EXPLORER and led wartime reporting from Iraq and Afghanistan. As head of production for Smithsonian Channel he exec-produced Cher & the Loneliest Elephant, 1,000 Years of Slavery and MLK: The Assassination Tapes. Recent work has included directing and writing the award-winning documentary short, Rosenwald: Toward A More Perfect Union and the one-hour Discovery special Tut’s Lost City Revealed.

speakers.name: Candace Y.A. Montague
speakers.bio:
Candace Y.A. Montague is a distinguished journalist based in Washington, DC, with 15 years of experience covering health, gender equality, and social justice for local and national publications. With degrees from Lincoln University and Trinity University, she’s committed to education and growth.

She received the Sigma Delta Chi Award in 2019 for her piece on parents coping with homicide loss in DC and the National Association of Black Journalists’ recognition in 2020 for her feature “Single Story.” In 2021, she was a finalist for the Dateline Award for Excellence in Local Journalism.

Candace’s commitment to diversity and investigative reporting earned her a fellowship at the Investigative Reporters and Editors Conference in 2022 and a spot in the Center For Health Journalism National Fellowship Program in 2023. In 2024, she won the Dateline Award for Excellence in Local Journalism for her series on Black infant mortality in DC. Her work amplifies marginalized voices and drives meaningful change.

speakers.name: Ray Whitehouse
speakers.bio:
Ray Whitehouse (he/him) is a documentary director of photography who lives in Washington, DC. He works at the intersection of documentary film and journalism, bringing a strong visual sensibility and commitment to journalistic principals to every project he works on. The core tenets of his practice are transparency, collaboration and critical reflexivity.

He’s worked as a cinematographer on more than 25 documentary features and filmed projects for The New York Times, The Washington Post, Univision, among others. He has more than a decade of experience covering political issues across the U.S.

He served as the Second Unit DP on To the End, directed by Rachel Lears, which premiered at Sundance in 2022.

He DP’d his feature-length directorial debut, A Run For More, which had its world premiere at Frameline in June 2022 and screened more than 30 festivals across the U.S. The film had its broadcast on PBS in 2023.

He served as a cinematographer and producer on 51st State, which premiered at DC DOX in 2024 and received a special jury award at DOC NYC.

Bring Them Home, a documentary short he co-directed and DP’d, premiered at the Big Sky Documentary Film Festival in 2022.

He was part of The Washington Post team that was awarded the Pulitzer Prize for reporting about the Capitol insurrection and its aftermath.

He is community coordinator for the D.C. chapter of Video Consortium and a member of the Documentary Cinematographers Alliance. He holds an M.A. in documentary journalism from UNC Chapel Hill and a B.S. in journalism from Northwestern University.

speakers.name: Nicole D’Arcangelo
speakers.bio: Nicole D’Arcangelo writes humorous non-fiction travel stories and fantasy novels. She is also a classically trained actor. She currently resides in the DC area and rescues stray cats to adopt out to their forever homes in here spare time. You can follow Nicole on Instagram @lildarcangel or visit her website at www.nicoledarcangelo.com

speakers.name: Wonjung Bae
speakers.bio: Wonjung Bae is a non-fiction storyteller/documentary filmmaker/news producer and lecturer at the Johns Hopkins University Graduate Program in Film and Media Studies. Bae made her first film, Grand, Father and Me, at age sixteen and has won numerous awards for her work, including the 38th Student Academy Award, the 16th Annual Directors Guild of America Student Film Award, and the Kodak Cinematographers Scholarship, among others.Before joining Johns Hopkins, Bae was the Seoul Producer for BBC covering stories including the South-North Korean division on land and mind, Korean women’s emerging voice against sexual violence, and the unprecedented challenges of the Covid-19 pandemic for the last seven years. Her team’s investigation on the Gangnam sex scandal was a winner at the Asian Academy Creative Awards for Best Single News Story/Report of Korea, 2019.Prior to the BBC, Bae led a production company specialized in international co-productions for character-driven social justice films. One of its features, Dollar Heroes, was shown at the European Parliament and the UN, and broadcasted through more than 70 public stations including BBC Panorama and Storyville as well as numerous international film festivals. The film was nominated for a 2019 Grierson Documentary Award for Best Documentary Series and won the 59th Monte-Carlo TV Festival Golden Nymph Awards for Best Documentary.Bae completed her MFA in Film and Video at Columbia College Chicago and her internship at PBS FRONTLINE, WGBH Boston. Bae cut her teeth in Chicago as a documentary editor for Emmy Award-winning producer Tod Lending and Kartemquin Films. Born in Busan, South Korea, Bae studied political science at Korea University for her undergraduate degree and is an aspiring flutist.

speakers.name: Kelsey Nicole Nelson
speakers.bio:
Kelsey Nicole Nelson is a host/reporter for FOX Sports Radio and is the founder, executive producer and host of the award-winning “Listen In With KNN” podcast where she runs two collegiate internship programs. She is also a lecturer at George Washington University in the School of Media and Public Affairs where she launched and teaches “Intro to Sports Writing and Reporting.” She also serves on the GW Athletics and Recreation Senate Committee. Kelsey has worked on a national level with Bally Sports, NBC/Peacock and the Draft Network. She’s also been featured on top networks in Dubai, London and Canada to discuss the latest sports topics. Kelsey also worked as a member of the Washington Commanders broadcast/digital teams. Sheen Magazine just recognized her as a trailblazing woman during Black History Month 2025.

Most recently, Kelsey was named to the 2025 class of Maryland’s Top 100 Women by The Daily Record and to The Daily Record’s Leading Women Under 40 class. She was also named Young Entrepreneur of the Year by the DC Chamber of Commerce and a Hometown Hero by SERVPRO and the University of Maryland. Kelsey was also named to the 2025 CORE 100 Most Influential Blacks Today and named one of the 50 Top Influential Women at the 2025 Black Excellence Awards. Kelsey is also a two-time recipient of the Presidential Lifetime Achievement Award and she was named to the 2023 Emerging Leaders Awards class by Washington Women in PR. Her achievement list also includes being presented with the highest honor by the Thursday Network (of the Greater Washington Urban League), being named a Luminary Award winner. Kelsey was also awarded by W.O.W. Magazine, the Black Entertainment Awards, the Black Girl Magic Alliance, the Next Generation Entertainment Awards and recognized as an honoree for the WKYS “Top 30 Under 30” class and named to the Terrapin Club 30 Under 30 Class of 2022. Kelsey has also been named D.C. Media Person of the Year and DMV Sports Media Person of the Year. She serves as a color commentator for the American University Women’s Basketball team and as a studio host for the Atlantic 10 Conference.

In addition to television, Kelsey has also been featured in numerous magazines for her work nationally and abroad. She is a former Vice President for the Washington Association of Black Journalists. Today, she serves as the Co-Chair of the communications committee for the National Capital Chesapeake Bay Chapter Emmy Awards of The National Academy of Television Arts & Sciences. She also sits on the board of the Montgomery County Sports Hall of Fame and on the advisory board for Period Reality. Kelsey also sits on the Washington, D.C. Regional Advisory Council of Tickets for Kids.

Speakers Magazine described her as a “rising star,” and she was named the Top Entrepreneurial Speaker at the 2025 Top Speakers Awards.

speakers.name: Benjamin Duchek
speakers.bio: Benjamin Duchek is a filmmaker and host of First Time Go podcast, a show highlighting independent filmmakers in the hopes of making it a little bit easier to get their films made and seen.

speakers.name: Robin Givhan
speakers.bio:
Robin Givhan is a Pulitzer Prize-winning former senior critic-at-large for The Washington Post, and author of Make It Ours: Crashing the Gate of Culture with Virgil Abloh,  which came out in June 2025. Make it Ours examines the ways in which Virgil Abloh changed the fashion industry and how the fashion industry transformed to allow an unconventional creative force like Abloh to flourish.

She is also the author of The Battle of Versailles: The Night American Fashion Stumbled Into The Spotlight And Made History.

Her journalism has also appeared in Harper’s Bazaar, Vogue, Essence, and New York magazine, The Daily Beast and the New Yorker, among other publications. I’ve contributed to several books including Runway Madness,  No Sweat: Fashion, Free Trade and The Rights of Garment Workers, and Thirty Ways of Looking at Hillary: Reflections by Women Writers. I’m also the author, along with The Washington Post photo staff, of Michelle: Her First Year as First Lady.

speakers.name: Ellen Nakashima
speakers.bio:
Ellen Nakashima covers intelligence and national security issues for The Washington Post. She has written about the security aspects of the U.S.-China relationship, the west’s response to Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, and classified intelligence leaks. She has been a member of three Pulitzer Prize-winning teams at The Post, including in 2022 for an investigation of the Jan. 6 assault on the U.S. Capitol, in 2018 for digging into Moscow’s efforts to influence the 2016 election, and in 2014 for exploring the hidden scope National Security Agency surveillance. She has been a White House correspondent, Southeast Asia bureau chief and co-authored a biography of Al Gore. She joined The Post in 1995.

Honors and Awards: Pulitzer Prize for Public Service, 2014; Gerald Loeb Award 2014, NSA stories; Society of American Business Editors and Writers enterprise award 2009, for the story “Banking Regulator Played Advocate over Enforcer”; Daily Californian Alumni Association Alumna of the Year, 2017; Pulitzer Prize for reporting on Russian interference in the 2016 presidential election, 2018; Pulitzer Prize for Public Service in 2022 for an investigation of the Jan. 6 assault on the U.S. Capitol.

speakers.name: Seth Stoughton
speakers.bio:
Seth Stoughton is a Professor at the University of South Carolina Joseph F. Rice School of Law, where he serves as the Faculty Director of the Excellence in Policing & Public Safety (EPPS) Program. He holds an affiliate position as a Professor in the university’s Department of Criminology and Criminal Justice.

Seth is a nationally renowned policing scholar. His research has appeared in leading academic journals, he is the principal co-author of Evaluating Police Uses of Force (NYU Press 2020), and he has written book chapters about police misconduct, the use of force, and use-of-force review.
